sections.h2: What should you know before selling a house in Phoenix, AZ?
sections.html:
Phoenix is the largest city in Arizona and the county seat of Maricopa County, so a house sale here involves the city, the county recorder and the county treasurer in the same transaction. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 1,665,481 residents, and the city covers about 518 square miles of land.

This page explains how the city is divided into villages, what the heat does to a house, how school districts overlap, the city's short-term rental permit, the deed steps in downtown Phoenix and the property tax dates.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about Phoenix homeowners and renters?
sections.html:
In Phoenix, 57.3 percent of homes are owner-occupied, and the median value of an owner-occupied home is $420,700 for 2020 to 2024. The table collects the figures a seller is likely to compare with nearby cities.

That owner-occupied rate is lower than Mesa's 64.4 percent, Peoria's 76.0 percent and Oro Valley's 76.4 percent. If your house is a rental, a tenant in place affects how and when it can be shown.

sections.h2: How is the city of Phoenix divided into villages?
sections.html:
Phoenix is divided into 15 urban villages, and each has a Village Planning Committee appointed by the mayor and City Council. The villages are Ahwatukee Foothills, Alhambra, Camelback East, Central City, Deer Valley, Desert View, Encanto, Estrella, Laveen, Maryvale, North Gateway, North Mountain, Paradise Valley, Rio Vista and South Mountain.

The committees hear rezoning cases, general plan amendments and text amendments, then pass a recommendation to the Planning Commission and the City Council. That matters if a buyer plans to change the use of your lot, because the case will pass through the village committee first.

Wikipedia traces the village model to the 1970s, when the Phoenix Concept 2000 plan split the city into nine original villages, each with a core where greater height and density were allowed. South Mountain separates Ahwatukee from the rest of the city, and Camelback Mountain, North Mountain, Sunnyslope Mountain and Piestewa Peak stand inside the developed area.

sections.h2: How did Phoenix grow into the largest city in Arizona?
sections.html:
Phoenix began as an agricultural community in 1867 and is now the fifth most populous city in the United States. It was incorporated on February 25, 1881, and became the capital of the Arizona Territory in 1889. Its canal system supported farming, and the "Five C's" of cotton, cattle, citrus, climate and copper anchored its early economy until after World War II, when high-tech companies moved in and air conditioning made the summers easier to live with.

Sun City, which opened in 1960, became a template for retirement communities. The housing market later fell hard in the subprime crisis: by early 2009 the median home price was about $150,000, down from a peak of $262,000 in 2007, according to Wikipedia.

sections.h2: What does extreme heat mean for a Phoenix house?
sections.html:
Phoenix has a hot desert climate, and buyers and inspectors treat the air conditioner and roof as major items. The city sees about 111 days a year with a high of at least 100 degrees, and highs reach 110 degrees on average 21 days a year. The record high is 122 degrees, set June 26, 1990.

Recent summers have been far above average. July 2023 averaged 102.7 degrees, with a streak of 31 days at 110 or higher, and 2024 brought 113 straight days of 100 degrees or more and a record 70 days at 110 or higher. The urban heat island also keeps nights warm: the daily normal low stays at or above 80 degrees for an average of 74 days each summer. Wikipedia notes that nearly all Phoenix homes have air conditioning.

Before listing, gather:

  • Service dates and invoices for each cooling unit.
  • The age of the roof and any repairs.
  • Records of shade, insulation or window work done to cut cooling costs.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve a Phoenix address?
sections.html:
A Phoenix address can fall in any of 33 school districts, because annexations over the years pulled many pre-existing districts inside the city limits. Twenty-one elementary districts, four high school districts and four unified districts cover the city, and well over 100 charter schools operate in it.

The Phoenix Union High School District, with more than 27,000 students and 16 schools, is one of the largest in the country. Glendale Union, Tempe Union and Tolleson Union serve only parts of Phoenix, and of the four unified districts only Paradise Valley covers Phoenix completely. Because the boundaries are tangled, confirm the district for the exact address with the district office before you describe a school zone.

sections.h2: Do Phoenix short-term rental permit rules affect a sale?
sections.html:
They do if the house has been rented short term, because Phoenix now requires a permit, not a registration. The change took effect November 6, 2023, after Arizona Senate Bill 1168 let cities set up a limited permit process. The city must issue or deny a permit within 7 days of receiving a complete application.

  • The initial and renewal fee is $250 per permit, and applications go through the SHAPE PHX portal.
  • The owner needs an Arizona Transaction Privilege Tax license and must update the rental status with the Maricopa County Assessor.
  • A Notice of Intent goes by certified mail to adjacent neighbors and to registered homeowners associations and neighborhood associations within 600 feet.
  • Court-adjudicated violations carry minimum penalties of $500, $1,000 and $3,500, and a permit can be suspended for 12 months after three violations in a year.
  • For a property with an accessory dwelling unit that received a certificate of occupancy on or after September 14, 2024, an owner who applies on or after April 4, 2026 must file a notarized attestation that the owner will live on the property.

Contact the city's short-term rental staff at vacation.rental@phoenix.gov or 602-534-9723 for the status of a particular permit.

sections.h2: How is a Phoenix sale recorded and taxed?
sections.html:
The deed is filed at the Maricopa County Recorder, 301 W Jefferson St, Suite 200, which is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. and takes in-person filings without an appointment. A deed needs an Affidavit of Property Value or an exemption code, and the standard fee is $30.00 per document. A.R.S. 11-1133 requires the buyer and seller to certify the price, parcel number and sale date.

Property tax follows A.R.S. 42-18052: half is due October 1 and half March 1, the first half is delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on November 1 and the second after 5:00 p.m. on May 1, and a bill of $100 or less is due October 1 and delinquent after December 31. The Maricopa County Treasurer publishes the same dates. November 1 has passed, so ask the treasurer or your title company whether the first half on your parcel has been paid.

sections.h2: How do people get around Phoenix?
sections.html:
Phoenix is organized on a flat street grid, and the freeway system ties its villages together. Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport serves more than 100 cities with nonstop flights, Phoenix-Mesa Gateway Airport in Mesa handles additional commercial traffic, and Valley Metro operates a 38.5 mile light rail system with an A Line and a B Line. Wikipedia reports that 3.38 percent of workers commute by public transit.

Where the house sits relative to a rail stop or a freeway on-ramp is a fair point to mention in a listing.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to rent my Phoenix house short term?
faqs.a: Yes. Phoenix requires a short-term rental permit from the Planning and Development Department, with a $250 initial and renewal fee. The owner also needs an Arizona Transaction Privilege Tax license and must notify neighbors by certified mail.

faqs.q: How many urban villages does Phoenix have?
faqs.a: Phoenix has 15 urban villages, from Ahwatukee Foothills to South Mountain. Each has a Village Planning Committee that reviews rezoning cases before they reach the Planning Commission.

faqs.q: Which county office records a Phoenix deed?
faqs.a: The Maricopa County Recorder at 301 W Jefferson St, Suite 200 in Phoenix. The deed needs an Affidavit of Property Value or an exemption code, and the standard fee is $30.00 per document.

faqs.q: When are Phoenix property taxes due?
faqs.a: Half is due October 1 and half is due March 1. The first half goes delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on November 1 and the second after 5:00 p.m. on May 1.

faqs.q: How many school districts serve Phoenix?
faqs.a: Phoenix is covered by 33 school districts, including 21 elementary districts, four high school districts and four unified districts. Ask the district to confirm the school for an exact address.
